sanskrit: kāñcanīṃ śirasā bibhrad bhīmasenaḥ srajaṃ śubhām bāṇakhaḍgadhanuṣpāṇir udaikṣata dhanādhipam
english: Wearing a golden garland on his head, Bhīmasena, with arrows, sword, and bow in hand, gazed up at the lord of wealth.

sanskrit: na bhīr bhīmasya na glānir vikṣatasyāpi rākṣasaiḥ āsīt tasyām avasthāyāṃ kuberam api paśyataḥ
english: Even wounded by the rākṣasas and now beholding Kubera himself, Bhīma felt neither fear nor fatigue in that moment.

sanskrit: ādadānaṃ śitān bāṇān yoddhukāmam avasthitam dṛṣṭvā bhīmaṃ dharmasutam abravīn naravāhanaḥ
english: Seeing Bhīma standing ready for battle, drawing sharp arrows, the son of Dharma was addressed by Naravāhana, the lord borne by men.

sanskrit: vidus tvāṃ sarvabhūtāni pārtha bhūtahite ratam nirbhayaś cāpi śailāgre vasa tvaṃ saha bandhubhiḥ
english: All beings know you, O Pārtha, as one devoted to their welfare. Dwell fearlessly on the mountaintop together with your kinsmen.

sanskrit: na ca manyus tvayā kāryo bhīmasenasya pāṇḍava kālenaite hatāḥ pūrvaṃ nimittam anujas tava
english: Do not be angry with Bhīmasena, O Pāṇḍava. These were slain by fate long before — your younger brother was merely the instrument.

sanskrit: vrīḍā cātra na kartavyā sāhasaṃ yad idaṃ kṛtam dṛṣṭaś cāpi suraiḥ pūrvaṃ vināśo yakṣarakṣasām
english: There is no cause for shame in this bold deed. The destruction of the yakṣas and rākṣasas had already been foreseen by the gods.

sanskrit: na bhīmasene kopo me prīto 'smi bharatarṣabha karmaṇānena bhīmasya mama tuṣṭir abhūt purā
english: I bear no anger toward Bhīmasena; rather, I am pleased, O bull of the Bharatas. By this very deed of Bhīma's, satisfaction had come to me before.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu rājānaṃ bhīmasenam abhāṣata naitan manasi me tāta vartate kurusattama yad idaṃ sāhasaṃ bhīma kṛṣṇārthe kṛtavān asi
english: Having spoken thus to the king, he then addressed Bhīmasena: 'This does not weigh on my mind, dear one, O best of the Kurus — this bold act you have done for Kṛṣṇā's sake, O Bhīma.'

sanskrit: mām anādṛtya devāṃś ca vināśaṃ yakṣarakṣasām svabāhubalam āśritya tenāhaṃ prītimāṃs tvayi śāpād asmi vinirmukto ghorād adya vṛkodara
english: Disregarding both me and the gods, relying solely on the strength of your own arms, you wrought the destruction of the yakṣas and rākṣasas — and for this I am pleased with you. Today, O Vṛkodara, I am released from a dreadful curse.

sanskrit: ahaṃ pūrvam agastyena kruddhena paramarṣiṇā śapto 'parādhe kasmiṃś cit tasyaiṣā niṣkṛtiḥ kṛtā
english: Long ago I was cursed by the great sage Agastya in his anger for some transgression; the expiation of that curse has now been accomplished.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭo hi mama saṃkleśaḥ purā pāṇḍavanandana na tavātrāparādho 'sti kathaṃ cid api śatruhan
english: My affliction was foreseen long before, O joy of the Pāṇḍavas. In this matter there is no fault of yours in any way, O slayer of foes.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ śapto 'si bhagavann agastyena mahātmanā śrotum icchāmy ahaṃ deva tavaitac chāpakāraṇam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How were you cursed, O blessed one, by the great-souled Agastya? I wish to hear, O god, the cause of that curse.

sanskrit: idaṃ cāścaryabhūtaṃ me yat krodhāt tasya dhīmataḥ tadaiva tvaṃ na nirdagdhaḥ sabalaḥ sapadānugaḥ
english: And this too is a wonder to me — that you were not instantly consumed along with your whole army and retinue by the fury of that wise sage.

sanskrit: vaiśravaṇa uvāca devatānām abhūn mantraḥ kuśavatyāṃ nareśvara vṛtas tatrāham agamaṃ mahāpadmaśatais tribhiḥ yakṣāṇāṃ ghorarūpāṇāṃ vividhāyudhadhāriṇām
english: Vaiśravaṇa said: A council of the gods was held at Kuśavatī, O lord of men. I went there attended by three hundred great-padma hosts of yakṣas of fearsome forms, bearing diverse weapons.

sanskrit: adhvany aham athāpaśyam agastyam ṛṣisattamam ugraṃ tapas tapasyantaṃ yamunātīram āśritam nānāpakṣigaṇākīrṇaṃ puṣpitadrumaśobhitam
english: On the road I came upon the foremost of sages, Agastya, performing fierce austerities on the bank of the Yamunā, that place thronged with flocks of birds and adorned with flowering trees.

sanskrit: tam ūrdhvabāhuṃ dṛṣṭvā tu sūryasyābhimukhaṃ sthitam tejorāśiṃ dīpyamānaṃ hutāśanam ivaidhitam
english: Seeing him standing with arms raised, facing the sun, a mass of radiance blazing like a kindled fire —

sanskrit: rākṣasādhipatiḥ śrīmān maṇimān nāma me sakhā maurkhyād ajñānabhāvāc ca darpān mohāc ca bhārata nyaṣṭhīvad ākāśagato maharṣes tasya mūrdhani
english: — Maṇimān, the glorious lord of rākṣasas, my companion, out of foolishness, ignorance, arrogance, and delusion, spat from the sky upon the head of that great sage, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa kopān mām uvācedaṃ diśaḥ sarvā dahann iva mām avajñāya duṣṭātmā yasmād eṣa sakhā tava
english: In his rage he spoke to me, burning as if to scorch all directions: 'Because this companion of yours, this corrupt-souled one, has shown contempt for me —'

sanskrit: dharṣaṇāṃ kṛtavān etāṃ paśyatas te dhaneśvara tasmāt sahaibhiḥ sainyais te vadhaṃ prāpsyati mānuṣāt
english: '— and committed this outrage while you looked on, O lord of wealth, therefore he along with your armies shall meet death at the hands of a human.'

sanskrit: tvaṃ cāpy ebhir hataiḥ sainyaiḥ kleśaṃ prāpsyasi durmate tam eva mānuṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā kilbiṣād vipramokṣyase
english: 'And you too, O foolish one, shall suffer distress when these troops are slain; but upon seeing that very human, you shall be released from sin.'

sanskrit: sainyānāṃ tu tavaiteṣāṃ putrapautrabalānvitam na śāpaṃ prāpsyate ghoraṃ gaccha te ''jñāṃ kariṣyati
english: 'But your troops together with their sons and grandsons and strength shall not receive the terrible curse — go, he will do your bidding.'

sanskrit: eṣa śāpo mayā prāptaḥ prāk tasmād ṛṣisattamāt sa bhīmena mahārāja bhrātrā tava vimokṣitaḥ
english: This is the curse I received long ago from that foremost of sages; and it has now been discharged, O great king, by your brother Bhīma.

sanskrit: vaiśravaṇa uvāca yudhiṣṭhira dhṛtir dākṣyaṃ deśakālau parākramaḥ lokatantravidhānānām eṣa pañcavidho vidhiḥ
english: Vaiśravaṇa said: O Yudhiṣṭhira, steadiness, skill, place, time, and valor — these are the five means by which the affairs of the world are conducted.

sanskrit: dhṛtimantaś ca dakṣāś ca sve sve karmaṇi bhārata parākramavidhānajñā narāḥ kṛtayuge 'bhavan
english: In the Kṛta age, O Bhārata, men were steadfast and skilled, each in his own work, and knowledgeable in the conduct of valor.

sanskrit: dhṛtimān deśakālajñaḥ sarvadharmavidhānavit kṣatriyaḥ kṣatriyaśreṣṭha pṛthivīm anuśāsti vai
english: A kṣatriya who is steadfast, knows place and time, and understands all the ordinances of righteousness truly governs the earth, O best of kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: ya evaṃ vartate pārtha puruṣaḥ sarvakarmasu sa loke labhate vīra yaśaḥ pretya ca sadgatim
english: The man who conducts himself thus in all his actions, O Pārtha, attains fame in this world, O hero, and a good state after death.

sanskrit: deśakālāntaraprepsuḥ kṛtvā śakraḥ parākramam saṃprāptas tridive rājyaṃ vṛtrahā vasubhiḥ saha
english: Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, having striven for mastery of place and time, attained sovereignty in the three worlds together with the Vasus.

sanskrit: pāpātmā pāpabuddhir yaḥ pāpam evānuvartate karmaṇām avibhāgajñaḥ pretya ceha ca naśyati
english: He who is of evil soul and evil mind, who pursues only evil, ignorant of the distinctions in action, perishes both here and hereafter.

sanskrit: akālajñaḥ sudurmedhāḥ kāryāṇām aviśeṣavit vṛthācārasamārambhaḥ pretya ceha ca naśyati
english: He who does not know the right time, is of very dim understanding, cannot distinguish what ought to be done, and undertakes actions of vain conduct, perishes both here and hereafter.

sanskrit: sāhase vartamānānāṃ nikṛtīnāṃ durātmanām sarvasāmarthyalipsūnāṃ pāpo bhavati niścayaḥ
english: For those who live by rash boldness, who are deceitful, of evil soul, and greedy for all power, the resolve itself becomes sinful.

sanskrit: adharmajño 'valiptaś ca bālabuddhir amarṣaṇaḥ nirbhayo bhīmaseno 'yaṃ taṃ śādhi puruṣarṣabha
english: This Bhīmasena is ignorant of what is wrong, arrogant, childish in understanding, and intolerant of insult. Instruct him, O bull among men.

sanskrit: ārṣṭiṣeṇasya rājarṣeḥ prāpya bhūyas tvam āśramam tāmisraṃ prathamaṃ pakṣaṃ vītaśokabhayo vasa
english: Return again to the hermitage of the royal sage Ārṣṭiṣeṇa and dwell there free of sorrow and fear for the first dark fortnight.

sanskrit: alakāḥ saha gandharvair yakṣaiś ca saha rākṣasaiḥ manniyuktā manuṣyendra sarve ca girivāsinaḥ rakṣantu tvā mahābāho sahitaṃ dvijasattamaiḥ
english: The Alakas together with the Gandharvas, and the yakṣas along with the rākṣasas, appointed by me, and all the dwellers of the mountain, shall protect you, O mighty-armed one, together with the foremost of the twice-born.

sanskrit: sāhaseṣu ca saṃtiṣṭhann iha śaile vṛkodaraḥ vāryatāṃ sādhv ayaṃ rājaṃs tvayā dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: As for Vṛkodara, who persists in rash deeds on this mountain, restrain him well, O king, O best upholder of righteousness.

sanskrit: itaḥ paraṃ ca rājendra drakṣyanti vanagocarāḥ upasthāsyanti ca sadā rakṣiṣyanti ca sarvaśaḥ
english: From this time on, O lord of kings, the forest-ranging beings will see you, will attend upon you always, and will protect you on every side.

sanskrit: tathaiva cānnapānāni svādūni ca bahūni ca upasthāsyanti vo gṛhya matpreṣyāḥ puruṣarṣabha
english: And likewise, my servants shall bring and present to you sweet and abundant food and drink, O bull among men.

sanskrit: yathā jiṣṇur mahendrasya yathā vāyor vṛkodaraḥ dharmasya tvaṃ yathā tāta yogotpanno nijaḥ sutaḥ
english: As Jiṣṇu is of Mahendra, as Vṛkodara is of Vāyu, so are you, dear one, the son born of Dharma himself, a true offspring.

sanskrit: ātmajāv ātmasaṃpannau yamau cobhau yathāśvinoḥ rakṣyās tadvan mamāpīha yūyaṃ sarve yudhiṣṭhira
english: And the twin sons, both endowed with the qualities of the Aśvins, are like their own children — even so, you are all to be protected by me here, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: arthatattvavibhāgajñaḥ sarvadharmaviśeṣavit bhīmasenād avarajaḥ phalgunaḥ kuśalī divi
english: Phalguna, younger than Bhīmasena, who knows the true nature and distinctions of all purposes, and all the particularities of righteousness, fares well in heaven.

sanskrit: yāḥ kāś cana matā lokeṣv agryāḥ paramasaṃpadaḥ janmaprabhṛti tāḥ sarvāḥ sthitās tāta dhanaṃjaye
english: Whatever supreme excellences are recognized in the worlds as the highest attainments, all of them have resided in Dhanaṃjaya from birth, dear one.

sanskrit: damo dānaṃ balaṃ buddhir hrīr dhṛtis teja uttamam etāny api mahāsattve sthitāny amitatejasi
english: Self-restraint, generosity, strength, intelligence, modesty, steadiness, and supreme splendor — these too reside in that great being of boundless energy.

sanskrit: na mohāt kurute jiṣṇuḥ karma pāṇḍava garhitam na pārthasya mṛṣoktāni kathayanti narā nṛṣu
english: Jiṣṇu does not out of delusion perform any blameworthy act, O Pāṇḍava. Men do not report that Pārtha has spoken falsehood among men.

sanskrit: sa devapitṛgandharvaiḥ kurūṇāṃ kīrtivardhanaḥ mānitaḥ kurute 'strāṇi śakrasadmani bhārata
english: He, the increaser of the Kurus' glory, honored by gods, ancestors, and Gandharvas, is practicing the use of weapons in Indra's abode, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yo 'sau sarvān mahīpālān dharmeṇa vaśam ānayat sa śaṃtanur mahātejāḥ pitus tava pitāmahaḥ prīyate pārtha pārthena divi gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: That Śaṃtanu of great splendor, who brought all earth-lords under his sway by righteousness, your father's grandfather, O Pārtha, rejoices in heaven at Pārtha the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: samyak cāsau mahāvīryaḥ kuladhurya iva sthitaḥ pitṝn devāṃs tathā viprān pūjayitvā mahāyaśāḥ sapta mukhyān mahāmedhān āharad yamunāṃ prati
english: And that one of great valor and great fame, standing firm as the bearer of the family's yoke, having duly honored the ancestors, gods, and brāhmaṇas, performed seven great sacrifices on the Yamunā.

sanskrit: adhirājaḥ sa rājaṃs tvāṃ śaṃtanuḥ prapitāmahaḥ svargajic chakralokasthaḥ kuśalaṃ paripṛcchati
english: That Śaṃtanu, your great-grandfather, the overlord of kings, who has won heaven and dwells in Indra's world, inquires after your welfare, O king.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ śaktiṃ gadāṃ khaḍgaṃ dhanuś ca bharatarṣabha prādhvaṃ kṛtvā namaścakre kuberāya vṛkodaraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Vṛkodara, O bull of the Bharatas, laid down his spear, mace, sword, and bow, and bowed in obeisance to Kubera.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd dhanādhyakṣaḥ śaraṇyaḥ śaraṇāgatam mānahā bhava śatrūṇāṃ suhṛdāṃ nandivardhanaḥ
english: Then the lord of wealth, the refuge of the refuge-seeking, spoke to the one who had come for shelter: 'Be the destroyer of enemies' pride and the increaser of friends' joy.'

sanskrit: sveṣu veśmasu ramyeṣu vasatāmitratāpanāḥ kāmān upahariṣyanti yakṣā vo bharatarṣabhāḥ
english: 'While you dwell in your pleasant abodes, O scorchers of foes, O bulls of the Bharatas, the yakṣas shall bring and present to you your desires.'

sanskrit: śīghram eva guḍākeśaḥ kṛtāstraḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ sākṣān maghavatā sṛṣṭaḥ saṃprāpsyati dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: 'Very soon, Dhanaṃjaya, the bull among men, Guḍākeśa, having mastered all weapons, dispatched directly by Maghavat, will arrive.'

sanskrit: evam uttamakarmāṇam anuśiṣya yudhiṣṭhiram astaṃ girivaraśreṣṭhaṃ prayayau guhyakādhipaḥ
english: Having thus instructed Yudhiṣṭhira, who had done such noble deeds, the lord of the Guhyakas departed toward the best of mountains, Asta.

sanskrit: taṃ paristomasaṃkīrṇair nānāratnavibhūṣitaiḥ yānair anuyayur yakṣā rākṣasāś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: Thousands of yakṣas and rākṣasas followed him in vehicles covered with canopies and adorned with various gems.

sanskrit: pakṣiṇām iva nirghoṣaḥ kuberasadanaṃ prati babhūva paramāśvānām airāvatapathe yatām
english: Like the sound of birds there arose the sound of the excellent steeds on the path of Airāvata, moving toward Kubera's abode.

sanskrit: te jagmus tūrṇam ākāśaṃ dhanādhipativājinaḥ prakarṣanta ivābhrāṇi pibanta iva mārutam
english: The horses of the lord of wealth sped swiftly through the sky, as though dragging the clouds along, as though drinking in the wind.

sanskrit: tatas tāni śarīrāṇi gatasattvāni rakṣasām apākṛṣyanta śailāgrād dhanādhipatiśāsanāt
english: Then, by the command of the lord of wealth, the lifeless bodies of the rākṣasas were removed from the mountaintop.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ hi śāpakālo 'sau kṛto 'gastyena dhīmatā samare nihatās tasmāt sarve maṇimatā saha
english: For the wise Agastya had appointed that as the time of the curse upon them; therefore they were all slain in battle together with Maṇimān.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavās tu mahātmānas teṣu veśmasu tāṃ kṣapām sukham ūṣur gatodvegāḥ pūjitāḥ sarvarākṣasaiḥ
english: And the great-souled Pāṇḍavas spent that night in those dwellings in ease, free of anxiety, honored by all the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ sūryodaye dhaumyaḥ kṛtvāhnikam ariṃdama ārṣṭiṣeṇena sahitaḥ pāṇḍavān abhyavartata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then at sunrise, O subduer of foes, Dhaumya, having performed the daily rites, came to the Pāṇḍavas together with Ārṣṭiṣeṇa.

sanskrit: te 'bhivādyārṣṭiṣeṇasya pādau dhaumyasya caiva ha tataḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve brāhmaṇāṃs tān apūjayan
english: They bowed at the feet of Ārṣṭiṣeṇa and of Dhaumya; then all of them, with folded hands, honored those brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiraṃ dhaumyo gṛhītvā dakṣiṇe kare prācīṃ diśam abhiprekṣya maharṣir idam abravīt
english: Then the great sage Dhaumya, taking Yudhiṣṭhira by the right hand and gazing toward the eastern direction, spoke these words.

sanskrit: asau sāgaraparyantāṃ bhūmim āvṛtya tiṣṭhati śailarājo mahārāja mandaro 'bhivirājate
english: 'That king of mountains, Mandara, stands pervading the earth all the way to the ocean, O great king, and blazes forth in splendor.'

sanskrit: indravaiśravaṇāv etāṃ diśaṃ pāṇḍava rakṣataḥ parvataiś ca vanāntaiś ca kānanaiś copaśobhitām
english: 'Indra and Vaiśravaṇa guard this direction, O Pāṇḍava, which is adorned with mountains, forest borders, and groves.'

sanskrit: etad āhur mahendrasya rājño vaiśravaṇasya ca ṛṣayaḥ sarvadharmajñāḥ sadma tāta manīṣiṇaḥ
english: 'This is the abode of Mahendra and of King Vaiśravaṇa, dear one, as declared by the wise sages who know all righteousness.'

sanskrit: ataś codyantam ādityam upatiṣṭhanti vai prajāḥ ṛṣayaś cāpi dharmajñāḥ siddhāḥ sādhyāś ca devatāḥ
english: 'From this direction the rising sun is worshipped by people, and also by the sages who know righteousness, by the Siddhas, the Sādhyas, and the gods.'

sanskrit: yamas tu rājā dharmātmā sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ prabhuḥ pretasattvagatīm etāṃ dakṣiṇām āśrito diśam
english: 'King Yama, the righteous-souled lord of all breathing beings, occupies the southern direction, which is the path traveled by departed beings.'

sanskrit: etat saṃyamanaṃ puṇyam atīvādbhutadarśanam pretarājasya bhavanam ṛddhyā paramayā yutam
english: 'This is the sacred place of restraint, of exceedingly wonderful appearance — the dwelling of the king of the departed, furnished with supreme prosperity.'

sanskrit: yaṃ prāpya savitā rājan satyena pratitiṣṭhati astaṃ parvatarājānam etam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: 'That mountain king upon reaching which the sun, O king, rests in truth — this is what the wise call Asta, the western mountain.'

sanskrit: etaṃ parvatarājānaṃ samudraṃ ca mahodadhim āvasan varuṇo rājā bhūtāni parirakṣati
english: 'Dwelling by this king of mountains and the great ocean, King Varuṇa guards all living beings.'

sanskrit: udīcīṃ dīpayann eṣa diśaṃ tiṣṭhati kīrtimān mahāmerur mahābhāga śivo brahmavidāṃ gatiḥ
english: 'The illustrious Mahāmeru, O greatly blessed one, stands illuminating the northern direction, auspicious, the refuge of those who know Brahman.'

sanskrit: yasmin brahmasadaś caiva tiṣṭhate ca prajāpatiḥ bhūtātmā visṛjan sarvaṃ yat kiṃ cij jaṅgamāgamam
english: 'On it stands also the abode of Brahman, and there Prajāpati, the soul of all beings, pours forth all that is mobile and immobile.'

sanskrit: yān āhur brahmaṇaḥ putrān mānasān dakṣasaptamān teṣām api mahāmeruḥ sthānaṃ śivam anāmayam
english: 'Mahāmeru is also the auspicious, affliction-free abode of those called the mind-born sons of Brahman, Dakṣa the seventh among them.'

sanskrit: atraiva pratitiṣṭhanti punar atrodayanti ca sapta devarṣayas tāta vasiṣṭhapramukhāḥ sadā
english: 'Here the seven divine sages always come to rest and from here they always rise again, dear one — Vasiṣṭha foremost among them.'

sanskrit: deśaṃ virajasaṃ paśya meroḥ śikharam uttamam yatrātmatṛptair adhyāste devaiḥ saha pitāmahaḥ
english: 'Behold that lustrous region, the highest peak of Meru, where the Grandfather dwells in contentment of self, together with the gods.'

sanskrit: yam āhuḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ prakṛteḥ prakṛtiṃ dhruvam anādinidhanaṃ devaṃ prabhuṃ nārāyaṇaṃ param
english: 'He whom they call the immutable, the source of primal matter for all beings, the god without beginning or end, the supreme Lord Nārāyaṇa —'

sanskrit: brahmaṇaḥ sadanāt tasya paraṃ sthānaṃ prakāśate devāś ca yatnāt paśyanti divyaṃ tejomayaṃ śivam
english: '— beyond Brahman's own abode, that supreme station shines forth, and even the gods behold with effort that divine, auspicious realm made of pure radiance.'

sanskrit: atyarkānaladīptaṃ tat sthānaṃ viṣṇor mahātmanaḥ svayaiva prabhayā rājan duṣprekṣyaṃ devadānavaiḥ
english: 'That station of the great-souled Viṣṇu blazes more than the sun and fire; by its own radiance, O king, it is difficult to behold even for gods and dānavas.'

sanskrit: tad vai jyotīṃṣi sarvāṇi prāpya bhāsanti no 'pi ca svayaṃ vibhur adīnātmā tatra hy abhivirājate
english: 'All luminaries, having reached that place, shine — and yet it is the self-existent one of undepressed spirit who truly blazes forth there of his own accord.'

sanskrit: yatayas tatra gacchanti bhaktyā nārāyaṇaṃ harim pareṇa tapasā yuktā bhāvitāḥ karmabhiḥ śubhaiḥ
english: 'Ascetics go thither to Nārāyaṇa Hari with devotion, endowed with supreme austerity, purified by virtuous deeds.'

sanskrit: yogasiddhā mahātmānas tamomohavivarjitāḥ tatra gatvā punar nemaṃ lokam āyānti bhārata
english: 'Those great souls perfected in yoga, free from darkness and delusion, having gone there, do not return to this world again, O Bhārata.'

sanskrit: sthānam etan mahābhāga dhruvam akṣayam avyayam īśvarasya sadā hy etat praṇamātra yudhiṣṭhira
english: 'This station, O greatly blessed one, is the eternal, imperishable, undecaying abode of the Lord — bow to it always, Yudhiṣṭhira.'
